Online Return

Company tax return for your Pty Ltd

Every Australian company lodges its own tax return each year, even if it made a loss or didn’t trade. We prepare the financial statements and the company return, and review the transactions between the company and its directors, which is where most small company problems start.

Our fee

Quoted before we start

Fixed, based on the state of the books, and agreed in writing before any work begins.

Company tax rate

25% or 30%

25% for base rate entities with turnover under $50 million and mostly active income. 30% otherwise.

Who does it

A registered tax agent

BRS Advisory Pty Ltd, agent 26233684, CPA Australia Practice.

What’s included

  • Year-end financial statements: profit and loss and balance sheet
  • Company income tax return prepared and lodged
  • Franking account reconciled and dividends documented
  • Director loan accounts reviewed for Division 7A
  • PAYG instalment rate reviewed for the year ahead
  • Directors’ own returns lined up with company distributions

How it runs

  1. 01 Give us access to your accounting software, or send the bank statements.
  2. 02 We quote a fixed fee on what’s actually there.
  3. 03 We finalise the books, prepare the accounts and flag any loan or dividend issues.
  4. 04 You approve the accounts and return, and we lodge before the due date.

When a company return is due

Company due dates depend on the company’s size and lodgement history. When a registered agent lodges, most small companies fall due later than they would if the directors lodged themselves. New companies and companies with overdue returns can have earlier dates, so we confirm yours at the start rather than assume.

The issue we find most often

Money taken out of a company isn’t the director’s money until it’s paid as wages, a dividend or a properly documented loan. If a director draws funds and the loan isn’t repaid or put under a complying loan agreement by the time the return is lodged, Division 7A can treat the amount as an unfranked dividend. That can mean tax at the director’s marginal rate on money they may already have spent. We check the loan account every year before lodging, while it can still be fixed.

Dormant and loss-making companies

A company that didn’t trade still has to lodge, or tell the ATO a return isn’t necessary in a way that matches its circumstances. Losses are worth recording properly: whether they can be used in a later year depends on the company passing the continuity of ownership or business continuity tests. ASIC’s annual review fee is separate from the tax return and payable even when the company is dormant.

Get a quote

Tell us about the company and the state of its books, and we’ll come back with a fixed fee.
